newsitem.title: USA: Fed bars ex-BCCI official from U.S. banking.
newsitem.headline: Fed bars ex-BCCI official from U.S. banking.

text.p: The Federal Reserve on Tuesday announced it has permanently barred a former officer of scandal-ridden Bank of Credit and Commerce International from U.S. banking and fined him $37 million.
The Fed said Ghaith R. Pharaon, a Saudi Arabian resident, was "a former BCCI insider" and said it was acting against him "due to his illegal activities."
It said Pharaon acted illegally by acting as a secret nominee for BCCI when he acquired the Independence Bank of Encino, Calif, in 1985. The Independence Bank failed in January 1992.
The Fed noted in its written decision that Pharaon is the subject of criminal indictments issued by the U.S. department of Justice and by the New York County District Attorney.

During 1996, a 19-day administrative hearing against Pharaon was held by the Fed. Pharaon participated through his attorney but has not returned to the United States to personally contest criminal charges against him, the Fed said.

The Fed said that BCCI and Pharaon had signed a secret agreement for Pharaon to buy and hold 100 percent of the shares of Independence Bank at a time when BCCI knew it could not get U.S. regulators' approval to do so on its own.

But Pharaon was holding 85 percent of the Independence Bank stock on behalf of BCCI and its was BCCI that had funded Pharaon's acquisiton of the stock, the Fed said. It said the plan was for BCCI to eventually get regulatory approval to buy Independence Bank from Pharaon and set up a bank holding company for BCCI's operations under U.S. supervisions.

However, BCCI failed in July 1991, leaving billions of dollars in losses behind it worldwide. The Fed started action against Pharaon in September 1991 and Independence Bank itself failed in January 1992.
